claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy has a relatively coarse eutectic lamellar microstructure.
Cold deformation followed by controlled annealing can reduce eutectic lamellar spacing.
Cold deformation followed by controlled annealing can make the lamellar-spacing distribution more homogeneous.
Suitable deformation and annealing parameters can avoid unwanted phase transformations.
The proposed mechanical-property improvements are expected during room-temperature testing.
Thermo-mechanical processing will produce a refined and more uniformly distributed eutectic lamellar microstructure.
A refined and uniformly distributed lamellar microstructure will better balance deformation between the soft and hard phases.
Refined lamellar spacing increases strength through enhanced boundary strengthening.
Refined lamellar spacing increases strength through enhanced interactions between phases.
Refined lamellar spacing promotes more homogeneous plastic deformation.
More homogeneous plastic deformation improves ductility.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing will simultaneously increase yield or ultimate tensile strength and ductility relative to standard processing.
Under optimal conditions, the anticipated improvement relative to the baseline is approximately 20–30%.
The beneficial effects occur only within a specific thermo-mechanical processing window.
Excessive deformation can undermine the mechanical-property improvements.
Excessive annealing can cause phase coarsening or instability and thereby undermine the mechanical-property improvements.
The magnitude of improvement depends on alloy composition and processing conditions.
